cards.text: Psalm 112 opens with a "Hallelujah!" right out of the gate. Then the psalmist paints a picture of one kind of man and calls him blessed. A whole psalm about what a blessed life looks like? Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, so take notes for both of us.

cards.question: Who is the man this psalm calls blessed?

answers.text: The man who fears the LORD
The man who leads an army
The man who builds a city

cards.question: The man who fears the LORD greatly ___ in His commandments.

cards.text: Now the psalm zooms out past this one man to his kids, his grandkids, the WHOLE family tree. Me? I've got six cookie cutters and I'm STILL bragging about them.

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says the descendants of the man who fears the LORD will be mighty in the land.

cards.text: Then the psalm walks into his house, and wealth and riches are in it. Friend, my house was a drawer. The richest thing in there was an expired coupon that still believed in itself.

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says the riches in this man's house endure forever.

cards.text: Here's what lasts: his righteousness endures forever. And Psalm 111:3 said those same words about the LORD Himself: "His righteousness endures forever." (Ps 111:3)
Next, the psalm heads into the darkness. Friend, I KNOW darkness. It was my roommate for years, and it never paid rent ONCE.

cards.question: For the upright, the gracious, compassionate and righteous, ___ dawns in the darkness.
The psalm says it is well with a certain kind of man. What is he like?

answers.text: He is generous and lends freely
He saves every coin he earns
He keeps his money hidden away

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says this generous man, whose affairs are guided by justice, will one day be shaken.

cards.text: In fact, the righteous man will be remembered forever. Then the psalm brings up what every adult dreads: bad news, like your boss texting "Got a minute?" at eleven at night.

cards.question: The man who fears the LORD does not fear bad news. Why not?

answers.text: His heart trusts in the LORD
He has plenty of money saved

cards.text: The psalm says, "His heart is assured; he does not fear, until he looks in triumph on his foes." Me? One rattle of that drawer and I was diving under a takeout menu.

cards.question: This man doesn't keep his gifts to himself. He scatters them abroad to the ___.

cards.text: That line again: his righteousness endures forever. And his horn will be lifted high in honor, which is the EXACT opposite of getting slid to the back of a drawer.

cards.question: At the very end, the wicked man shows up, and he sees. How does the wicked man react?

answers.text: He is grieved and gnashes his teeth
He changes his ways and gives

cards.text: He will waste away. And the psalm ends right there, quiet: the desires of the wicked will perish.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "Psalm 112 opens with...", "Then the psalmist paints...", "A whole psalm about what a blessed life looks like?" and "Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer..."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question's own wording rules out the wrong answers. Only "light" can dawn, so "rain" and "silence" can be dismissed without reasoning about the psalm.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He never checks his messages" is modern and jokey next to the Bible-toned right answer "His heart trusts in the LORD", so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He has plenty of money saved" could be argued from Psalm 112:3 ("Wealth and riches are in his house"), which the baker was told on card 6.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences (the v8 quote, "Me?", "One rattle of that drawer...").

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new event in his backstory: Papa Dorin diving under a takeout menu whenever the drawer rattled. The backstory says they all held their breath when the drawer opened, and invented moments are only allowed around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
